coverage: All catalog labels, aliases, definitions, motion theses and distinctions exported for review. Lexical comparison covers every unordered pair across all sections. Targeted source inspection adjudicates semantic overlap; this is not a claim of fresh visual review of all 1,001 studies.

inventory.label: Wind Rose
inventory.definition: A meteorological wind rose summarizes how often wind comes from each direction and the corresponding speed ranges.
inventory.motionThesis: Twenty synthetic equal-duration readings accumulate into sorted radial speed bands; calm readings remain separate, and the completed distribution holds before replay.
inventory.distinction: The current count-scale meteorological study replaces the former cartographic interpretation. Synthetic data; direction means FROM, and radial length rather than area counts readings.

inventory.label: Histogram Binning
inventory.definition: A histogram counts observations within adjacent numeric intervals.
inventory.motionThesis: Value markers drop into their matching intervals and build bars one observation at a time.
inventory.distinction: Bin assignment and accumulation, without the Galton Board's bouncing pegs.

inventory.label: Empirical Cumulative Distribution
inventory.definition: The empirical cumulative distribution gives the fraction of observations at or below each value.
inventory.motionThesis: A threshold crosses sorted samples while a linked staircase rises by one equal increment per observation.
inventory.distinction: A cumulative threshold and staircase rather than disjoint bin heights.

inventory.label: Box Plot Quartiles
inventory.definition: A box plot summarizes ordered observations using the median, quartiles, whiskers, and possible outliers.
inventory.motionThesis: Ordered observations project onto quartile gates, a median, and whiskers spanning the non-outlying extremes.
inventory.distinction: Rank-to-summary geometry; this symmetric example has no Tukey outliers.

inventory.label: Bootstrap Resampling
inventory.definition: Bootstrapping estimates sampling variability by repeatedly sampling observed data with replacement.
inventory.motionThesis: Copies of source observations fill resample rows, including repeated selections, before each row yields a mean.
inventory.distinction: Source observations remain available after copying, unlike new population sampling or held-out folds.

inventory.label: Confidence Interval Coverage
inventory.definition: A confidence procedure produces intervals that cover a fixed parameter at a specified long-run rate.
inventory.motionThesis: Repeated sample intervals appear across a fixed truth line, with both covering and missing intervals retained.
inventory.distinction: The parameter stays fixed; the small illustrative sample does not claim an exact coverage percentage.

inventory.label: Central Limit Theorem
inventory.definition: Under suitable conditions, standardized averages of independent samples approach a normal distribution.
inventory.motionThesis: Samples from a skewed distribution collapse to means that accumulate into a more symmetric distribution below.
inventory.distinction: Shows averaging explicitly, rather than reusing the Galton Board or a thermal distribution.

inventory.label: Law of Large Numbers
inventory.definition: For independent identically distributed observations with a finite mean, sample averages converge toward that mean.
inventory.motionThesis: Several irregular running averages extend toward a common expectation while retaining late fluctuations.
inventory.distinction: Convergence of running estimates rather than the shape of a distribution of averages.

inventory.label: Bayesian Updating
inventory.definition: Bayesian inference combines prior probabilities with the likelihood of evidence to obtain posterior probabilities.
inventory.motionThesis: Evidence retains unequal fractions of two prior groups, then the surviving areas expand into a normalized posterior.
inventory.distinction: Area conditioning and renormalization, rather than a generic narrowing bell curve.

inventory.label: Poisson Arrival Process
inventory.definition: A homogeneous Poisson process models independent arrivals with a constant average rate.
inventory.motionThesis: Irregularly spaced arrivals cross successive equal time windows and produce different event counts.
inventory.distinction: A fixed realization of random event timing rather than periodic pulses.

inventory.label: Markov Chain
inventory.definition: A Markov chain changes state with probabilities determined by its current state.
inventory.motionThesis: Each state's probability bar retains half its mass and transfers half to its cyclic successor, conserving total probability.
inventory.distinction: Visible splitting and recombination of probability, rather than decorative traffic on a graph.

inventory.label: Absorbing Random Walk
inventory.definition: An absorbing random walk stops on reaching an absorbing state such as a boundary.
inventory.motionThesis: Walkers take discrete left or right steps along separate tracks and remain fixed after reaching either end barrier.
inventory.distinction: Explicit discrete steps and permanent boundary capture distinguish it from Brownian Motion.

inventory.label: Monte Carlo Area Estimation
inventory.definition: Monte Carlo integration can estimate an area's fraction of a bounding region from randomly sampled point membership.
inventory.motionThesis: Uniform sample locations reveal inside or outside membership, and a matching tally forms the sampled area fraction.
inventory.distinction: Geometric membership contributes to an explicit fraction; points are not decorative particles.

inventory.label: Rejection Sampling
inventory.definition: Rejection sampling accepts proposals according to a target density bounded by a proposal envelope.
inventory.motionThesis: Candidates under a horizontal envelope either fall to the sample strip when beneath the target curve or remain crossed out above it.
inventory.distinction: Accepted horizontal positions become samples, unlike counting a geometric area fraction.

inventory.label: Metropolis Sampling
inventory.definition: The Metropolis algorithm forms a sampling chain by accepting or rejecting proposals using a target-density ratio.
inventory.motionThesis: A current sample proposes neighboring positions; accepted moves advance the chain, while a rejected move retains and records the old position.
inventory.distinction: Rejection repeats the current state rather than discarding an independent candidate.

inventory.label: Kernel Density Estimation
inventory.definition: Kernel density estimation sums smooth kernels centered on observed samples to estimate a probability density.
inventory.motionThesis: Individual sample-centered kernels contribute successively to a correctly summed density curve.
inventory.distinction: Kernel superposition, rather than histogram bins or a distribution of sample averages.

inventory.label: Autocorrelation
inventory.definition: Autocorrelation measures association between a time series and lagged copies of itself.
inventory.motionThesis: A shifted copy of a finite signed sequence aligns and opposes its original, while each lag's normalized correlation is recorded below.
inventory.distinction: Lagged comparison with signed products rather than generic wave interference.

inventory.label: Gradient Descent
inventory.definition: Gradient descent minimizes a differentiable function by taking steps opposite its local gradient.
inventory.motionThesis: Steps on elongated quadratic contours alternate across the steep direction while converging toward the minimum.
inventory.distinction: Computed optimization steps on an objective surface, rather than physical rolling or pendulum motion.

inventory.label: Projected Gradient Descent
inventory.definition: Projected gradient descent combines gradient steps with projection back onto a feasible constraint set.
inventory.motionThesis: Trial steps approach an unconstrained minimum outside a feasible rectangle, then projections return them to the constrained optimum.
inventory.distinction: Separates unconstrained trial motion from feasibility correction.

inventory.label: Simplex Linear Programming
inventory.definition: The simplex method improves a linear objective by moving between vertices of the feasible polytope.
inventory.motionThesis: A candidate pivots along polygon edges as parallel objective lines advance toward the best feasible vertex.
inventory.distinction: Vertex pivots and supporting objective lines, rather than continuous gradient paths.

inventory.label: Simulated Annealing
inventory.definition: Simulated annealing searches by progressively reducing the probability of accepting worse candidate solutions.
inventory.motionThesis: A six-city tour accepts an early longer detour, then improves and rejects a later longer proposal as temperature falls.
inventory.distinction: Discrete route rearrangements and a cooling acceptance schedule, rather than Metropolis density sampling.

inventory.label: Pareto Frontier
inventory.definition: A Pareto frontier contains feasible solutions for which improving one objective requires worsening another.
inventory.motionThesis: Dominance rectangles dim inferior candidate points and reveal the remaining nondominated samples.
inventory.distinction: Retains multiple incomparable optima instead of selecting a single best scalar objective.

inventory.label: Least-Squares Regression
inventory.definition: Least-squares regression fits model parameters by minimizing the sum of squared prediction residuals.
inventory.motionThesis: A line adjusts through fixed observations while squares on its vertical residuals reach their least total area.
inventory.distinction: Residual-square geometry explicitly encodes the objective being minimized.

inventory.label: Principal Component Analysis
inventory.definition: Principal component analysis finds orthogonal directions of greatest variance in centered data.
inventory.motionThesis: An axis rotates through a centered elongated cloud and settles on the maximum-variance direction before projecting the points onto it.
inventory.distinction: Variance along an orthogonal projection, rather than regression's vertical prediction residuals.

inventory.label: K-Means Clustering
inventory.definition: K-means alternates assignment to the nearest centroid with recomputation of cluster means.
inventory.motionThesis: Points first join the nearer centroid, then centroid crosses move to their assigned means before the next assignment.
inventory.distinction: Assignment and mean recomputation are separate visible phases.

inventory.label: DBSCAN Clustering
inventory.definition: DBSCAN builds clusters through dense neighborhoods and marks unreachable sparse observations as noise.
inventory.motionThesis: Overlapping fixed-radius neighborhoods extend a curved cluster, while an isolated observation remains outside the connected dense region.
inventory.distinction: Density connectivity, rather than moving centroids or straight separating lines.

inventory.label: Agglomerative Clustering
inventory.definition: Agglomerative clustering repeatedly merges the closest clusters under a chosen linkage criterion.
inventory.motionThesis: Point groups merge under single linkage while a matching dendrogram records the increasing merge distances.
inventory.distinction: A nested hierarchy of merges, rather than a flat final clustering.

inventory.label: Decision Tree Partition
inventory.definition: A decision tree predicts by recursively splitting feature space using tests.
inventory.motionThesis: A vertical split followed by conditional horizontal splits divides observations as the corresponding tree branches grow.
inventory.distinction: Recursive conditional regions, rather than global distance-based cluster assignments.

inventory.label: Support Vector Margin
inventory.definition: A linearly separable support-vector classifier selects a separating boundary with maximum margin.
inventory.motionThesis: A pair of parallel margin rails expands until the nearest opposing observations become its support contacts.
inventory.distinction: Nearest-class constraints set a separation margin; no regression line or centroid is fitted.

inventory.label: Nearest-Neighbor Classification
inventory.definition: A nearest-neighbor classifier predicts from the labels of the closest training observations.
inventory.motionThesis: A query's radius grows to enclose three nearest neighbors, whose shape-coded votes determine the query's class.
inventory.distinction: Local voting around a query, without learning a centroid or global separator.

inventory.label: K-Fold Cross-Validation
inventory.definition: K-fold cross-validation rotates held-out subsets to evaluate models trained on the remaining observations.
inventory.motionThesis: Five folds alternate as the held-out block, following a separate evaluation route that never enters the training funnel.
inventory.distinction: Training and test roles rotate without replacement within a fold, unlike bootstrap resampling.

inventory.label: ROC Threshold Sweep
inventory.definition: A receiver operating characteristic curve plots true-positive against false-positive rates as a classification threshold changes.
inventory.motionThesis: A threshold crosses positive and negative score observations while the corresponding count increments trace an exact stepped ROC curve.
inventory.distinction: Linked score threshold and conditional rates, rather than an arbitrary performance trace.

inventory.label: Confusion Matrix
inventory.definition: A confusion matrix counts the combinations of true and predicted classes.
inventory.motionThesis: Observations with independent inner truth shapes and outer prediction shapes sort into their matching four matrix cells.
inventory.distinction: Two-way categorical agreement uses shape as well as color and does not depend on tiny class labels.

inventory.label: Binary Search
inventory.definition: Binary search locates a key in sorted data by repeatedly discarding the half excluded by a midpoint comparison.
inventory.motionThesis: A midpoint probe compares increasing bars to a target height as brackets contract to the matching key.
inventory.distinction: Search bounds contract while the ordered data stays in place.

inventory.label: Merge Sort
inventory.definition: Merge sort orders data by merging sorted subsequences produced through recursive division or successive passes.
inventory.motionThesis: The smaller of two ordered input heads repeatedly moves into the next output slot in a merge-sort pass.
inventory.distinction: Two source fronts feed a separate ordered destination; keys never swap around a pivot.

inventory.label: Quicksort Partition
inventory.definition: A quicksort partition places a pivot between values smaller and larger than it before recursive sorting.
inventory.motionThesis: A scan swaps qualifying keys into the smaller-value region, then exchanges the pivot into the partition boundary.
inventory.distinction: One explicit partition of a single array rather than a claim to show the entire recursive sort.

inventory.label: Breadth-First Search
inventory.definition: Breadth-first search uses a first-in-first-out frontier to discover vertices in increasing unweighted distance from a source.
inventory.motionThesis: A queue admits newly discovered neighbors at its tail and removes the front vertex while the discovery tree grows by distance layer.
inventory.distinction: A visible FIFO frontier and duplicate-discovery skip distinguish traversal from a decorative radial pulse.

inventory.label: Dijkstra Shortest Path
inventory.definition: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths with nonnegative edge weights by settling the smallest tentative distance and relaxing outgoing edges.
inventory.motionThesis: Tentative distance bars shrink when a cheaper route is found, and predecessor links change before each minimum-distance vertex is settled.
inventory.distinction: Weighted relaxation and revisable predecessor links rather than unweighted discovery layers.

inventory.label: Kruskal Spanning Tree
inventory.definition: Kruskal's algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree by accepting the lightest available edges that join different components.
inventory.motionThesis: A sorted edge tray offers edges in increasing weight, rejects a triangle-closing edge, and completes the connecting tree.
inventory.distinction: Greedy edge selection with cycle rejection, rather than shortest paths from a source.

inventory.label: Union-Find
inventory.definition: Union-find represents disjoint sets using roots, with path compression shortening parent chains during find operations.
inventory.motionThesis: A find traverses a parent chain and redirects its links to the root, then a union joins two roots and a second find flattens the remaining chain.
inventory.distinction: Internal parent pointers change while set membership is preserved during compression.

inventory.label: Binary Heap
inventory.definition: A binary max-heap stores a complete binary tree whose parent keys are at least as large as their children.
inventory.motionThesis: A new maximum swims through parent exchanges to the root, then removal replaces it with the last key and sinks that key to restore heap order.
inventory.distinction: Local priority exchanges preserve a complete tree rather than rebalancing a search tree.

inventory.label: Radix Sort
inventory.definition: Least-significant-digit radix sort orders keys through stable digit-based passes from the least to the most significant position.
inventory.motionThesis: Four decimal keys enter units buckets in arrival order, return as a stable run, and repeat for the tens digit to finish sorted.
inventory.distinction: Stable distribution by one digit at a time rather than pairwise value comparisons.

inventory.label: AVL Tree Rotation
inventory.definition: An AVL tree rotation restores subtree-height balance while preserving binary-search key order.
inventory.motionThesis: A left-heavy tree rotates its left child into the root and transfers the middle subtree to the former root while the inorder sequence remains fixed.
inventory.distinction: Nodes and parent links move structurally; keys are not exchanged in a fixed heap shape.

inventory.label: Linear-Probing Hash Table
inventory.definition: Linear probing resolves a hash collision by examining consecutive slots, wrapping around the table until it finds a matching key or an empty slot.
inventory.motionThesis: Key 22 hashes to slot four in a six-slot table, encounters keys 10 and 16, wraps from slot five to zero, and enters the empty slot.
inventory.distinction: Explicit collision handling and cyclic array probing rather than a generic storage animation.

inventory.label: Prefix Trie
inventory.definition: A trie stores keys along symbol paths, sharing common prefixes and marking complete keys separately.
inventory.motionThesis: Inserting CAT and CAR reuses the C–A prefix before branching at their final characters, while DOG builds a separate path.
inventory.distinction: Symbol-by-symbol prefix sharing with terminal markers rather than ordered numeric tree comparisons.

inventory.label: Topological Sort
inventory.definition: A topological ordering places each vertex of a directed acyclic graph before all of its outgoing neighbors.
inventory.motionThesis: Removing ready vertices releases prerequisite pins, and a vertex enters the output only after its final incoming constraint disappears.
inventory.distinction: Dependency release and zero-indegree readiness rather than shortest-distance graph discovery.

inventory.label: Augmenting-Path Max Flow
inventory.definition: An augmenting-path method increases source-to-sink flow through residual capacity, including reverse edges that cancel earlier assignments.
inventory.motionThesis: A first unit crosses a middle edge, then a reverse residual step cancels that allocation and opens two disjoint unit-capacity routes to the sink.
inventory.distinction: Flow conservation, capacity use, and explicit cancellation rather than a routing highlight.

inventory.label: A* Search
inventory.definition: A* expands the frontier state with minimum estimated total cost, combining accumulated path cost with a heuristic estimate to the goal.
inventory.motionThesis: A grid frontier compares accumulated and Manhattan-estimated costs around a barrier before reconstructing the route when the goal is selected.
inventory.distinction: An explicit goal heuristic and spatial obstacle search rather than Dijkstra's weighted-network distance revisions.

inventory.label: Backtracking Maze
inventory.definition: Backtracking explores candidate solutions and retracts unsuccessful choices to continue from an earlier branch.
inventory.motionThesis: A route enters two walled dead ends, retracts along its own corridor, and keeps the successful path to the exit.
inventory.distinction: Physical corridor constraints and visible undoing of a route, with graph-stack traversal reserved for depth-first search.

inventory.label: Depth-First Search
inventory.definition: Depth-first search recursively explores unvisited neighbors before returning to the preceding vertex.
inventory.motionThesis: Call frames push and pop beside a graph while discovery edges remain and completed vertices enter a finish-order strip.
inventory.distinction: An explicit recursion stack and completion order rather than retracting a route through physical maze corridors.

inventory.label: Knapsack Dynamic Programming
inventory.definition: The 0–1 knapsack problem maximizes selected item value within a weight capacity, using each item at most once.
inventory.motionThesis: A capacity table compares inclusion with exclusion using previous-row states, then traces back two items that exactly fill capacity five.
inventory.distinction: A discrete include-or-exclude recurrence with reduced-capacity dependencies.

inventory.label: Edit Distance
inventory.definition: Levenshtein distance is the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, and substitutions between two strings.
inventory.motionThesis: Prefix-pair costs fill a table before a two-edit traceback changes CAT to CUT and then CUTS.
inventory.distinction: Character-operation costs and prefix alignment rather than item capacity selection.

inventory.label: Finite-State Automaton
inventory.definition: A deterministic finite automaton consumes symbols through finite state transitions and accepts according to its state when input ends.
inventory.motionThesis: Ones toggle even and odd parity states while zeros take self-loops, accepting an input with an even number of ones.
inventory.distinction: Two states alone retain parity, with no growing counter or stack.

inventory.label: Pushdown Automaton
inventory.definition: A pushdown automaton combines finite control with a stack whose top can be inspected and changed by transitions.
inventory.motionThesis: Typed opening brackets push three stack symbols, and matching closing brackets pop them in reverse order before acceptance at end of input.
inventory.distinction: Typed last-in-first-out memory changes while the processing control state stays fixed.

inventory.label: KMP String Search
inventory.definition: KMP uses a pattern's prefix structure to continue matching after a mismatch without moving the text position backward.
inventory.motionThesis: A mismatch holds the text cursor fixed while the pattern shifts two positions and retains its already matched ABA prefix.
inventory.distinction: Failure-link reuse of matched symbols, rather than naive retries or a generic automaton diagram.

inventory.label: Bloom Filter
inventory.definition: A Bloom filter sets several hashed bits per insertion; a missing query bit proves absence while all matching bits indicate possible membership.
inventory.motionThesis: Two keys populate shared bits, then an uninserted key gets a possible-membership result while another query hits a zero bit and is excluded.
inventory.distinction: An explicit false positive and definite negative distinguish probabilistic membership from exact hash-table storage.

inventory.label: Quadtree Subdivision
inventory.definition: A planar quadtree recursively divides regions into four child quadrants to organize spatial data.
inventory.motionThesis: The third point splits a capacity-two root, then a crowded child alone subdivides at its midpoint while empty quadrants remain.
inventory.distinction: Adaptive four-way spatial subdivision rather than decision-tree binary tests or global clustering.

inventory.label: Convex Hull
inventory.definition: The convex hull is the smallest convex set containing a collection of points.
inventory.motionThesis: An angular scan grows a candidate boundary, removes the interior vertex that creates a non-convex turn, and closes the hull.
inventory.distinction: Geometric orientation tests remove a concavity rather than selecting weighted graph edges.

inventory.label: Huffman Coding
inventory.definition: Huffman coding repeatedly combines the two least frequent nodes to construct a binary prefix code with minimum weighted codeword length.
inventory.motionThesis: The lowest weights merge upward into a coding tree, then unequal-length bit paths trace back to their symbols.
inventory.distinction: Frequency-driven bottom-up merges create unequal code lengths rather than sharing existing word prefixes in a trie.

inventory.label: Run-Length Encoding
inventory.definition: Run-length encoding represents each contiguous run of identical symbols by its length and, when needed, its symbol value.
inventory.motionThesis: A scan brackets a binary stream's consecutive runs and emits counts four, three, and two with their corresponding zero or one values.
inventory.distinction: Only adjacent repetition is grouped; no dictionary phrases or global frequency tree are built.

inventory.label: LZW Dictionary Coding
inventory.definition: LZW emits codes for longest dictionary phrases while extending the dictionary with each matched phrase plus the next input symbol.
inventory.motionThesis: ABABABA parses into A, B, AB, and ABA as phrase entries grow and the final output reuses the newest dictionary code.
inventory.distinction: Adaptive multi-symbol phrase reuse rather than grouping identical neighboring symbols.

inventory.label: Arithmetic Coding
inventory.definition: Arithmetic coding represents a message by successively narrowing a numeric interval according to symbol probabilities.
inventory.motionThesis: The known three-symbol message BAC selects nested intervals in a fixed probability model, yielding binary prefix 10011 through explicitly zoomed subdivisions.
inventory.distinction: One whole-message interval rather than an independent prefix-tree codeword per symbol.

inventory.label: Hamming Error Correction
inventory.definition: A Hamming code uses parity-check redundancy to locate and correct a single flipped bit.
inventory.motionThesis: Three parity masks identify flipped position six through syndrome 110, then restoring that bit returns the syndrome to zero.
inventory.distinction: Failed checks locate an unknown erroneous bit rather than recovering a known missing symbol.

inventory.label: Reed–Solomon Erasure Recovery
inventory.definition: Reed–Solomon erasure decoding recovers a degree-bounded polynomial from enough surviving finite-field evaluations to reconstruct missing symbols.
inventory.motionThesis: Three surviving evaluations recover a quadratic's coefficients modulo seven and regenerate the two known missing coded symbols.
inventory.distinction: Known erasures of whole field symbols, with no misleading real-valued curve or claim that the first packets are original data.

inventory.label: Merkle Tree
inventory.definition: A Merkle tree recursively hashes ordered child digests so a root commits to data and sibling paths support membership proofs.
inventory.motionThesis: Sibling hashes verify C's root path, then changing C to X updates only that leaf and its ancestors while the other digests remain fixed.
inventory.distinction: Fixed SHA-256 commitments and selective ancestor updates; displayed four-digit prefixes abbreviate full digests.

inventory.label: Shannon Entropy
inventory.definition: Shannon entropy is expected self-information, measured as the probability-weighted sum of negative base-two log probabilities.
inventory.motionThesis: Four exact distributions show probability widths times surprisal heights, with their total areas representing zero, one, one-and-a-half, and two bits.
inventory.distinction: Probability times information area, rather than a frequency histogram receiving observations.

inventory.label: Convolutional Encoder
inventory.definition: A convolutional encoder produces redundant output streams from input bits and finite memory through binary convolution.
inventory.motionThesis: Two XOR tap paths compute a pair from the current input and old register contents before the memory shifts and tail zeros flush it.
inventory.distinction: Streaming finite-memory redundancy, rather than block parity repair or a diagram with only abstract states.

inventory.label: TCP Three-Way Handshake
inventory.definition: TCP's three-way handshake synchronizes initial sequence numbers and establishes a connection through SYN, SYN plus ACK, and ACK segments.
inventory.motionThesis: Three ordered exchanges acknowledge each peer's initial sequence number, with the server becoming established only after the final acknowledgment arrives.
inventory.distinction: Connection establishment and sequence synchronization; the other TCP tiles show data transfer rather than repeating this setup ladder.

inventory.label: TCP Sliding Window
inventory.definition: TCP receive-window flow control bounds outstanding byte sequence space using receiver-advertised credit and cumulative acknowledgments.
inventory.motionThesis: A fixed four-cell credit bracket advances only after cumulative acknowledgments arrive, releasing room while older unacknowledged cells remain in flight.
inventory.distinction: Receiver byte credit moves across a fixed sequence rail; it does not show the network-congestion limit.

inventory.label: TCP Congestion Avoidance
inventory.definition: Classic TCP Reno increases its congestion window during acknowledged avoidance rounds and reduces its sending limit following congestion.
inventory.motionThesis: A window grows from four to eight segments, enters fast recovery at seven after three duplicate acknowledgments, deflates to four on recovery acknowledgment, then grows again.
inventory.distinction: An explicit Reno congestion-avoidance fixture, including its temporary fast-recovery window; this is not a claim about every TCP variant.

inventory.label: TCP Selective Acknowledgment
inventory.definition: TCP selective acknowledgments report noncontiguous received byte ranges in addition to the cumulative acknowledgment.
inventory.motionThesis: Two received islands leave holes in a byte buffer, and retransmitting only those holes lets the cumulative acknowledgment jump across retained data.
inventory.distinction: Sparse receive ranges and targeted hole repair, rather than a moving credit bracket; SACK information itself does not detect loss.

inventory.label: Recursive DNS Resolution
inventory.definition: A recursive DNS resolver obtains a final answer for its client by using cached data or querying name servers and following referrals.
inventory.motionThesis: A resolver follows root and top-level referrals, receives an authoritative answer, and caches it that satisfies a second request locally.
inventory.distinction: Resolver-centered referral traversal and a cache shortcut, rather than endpoint connection establishment.

inventory.label: DHCP Address Lease
inventory.definition: DHCP assigns network configuration for a finite lease period and supports renewal before that lease expires.
inventory.motionThesis: A discover, offer, request, and acknowledgment establish an eight-hour lease whose four-hour renewal extends its expiry to twelve hours from the initial request.
inventory.distinction: Address assignment and a renewed validity interval; ARP instead discovers a link-layer address for an already known IP address.

inventory.label: ARP Address Resolution
inventory.definition: ARP resolves an on-link protocol address to a link-layer address so an IPv4 packet can be encapsulated for local delivery.
inventory.motionThesis: A broadcast asks all local peers for a known IP address, the matching peer replies, and a cached mapping guides a later unicast frame.
inventory.distinction: Local broadcast discovery followed by link-layer unicast; no address assignment or router traversal.

inventory.label: Longest-Prefix Routing
inventory.definition: IP forwarding selects the most specific prefix among eligible routes matching a packet destination.
inventory.motionThesis: A destination matches several nested network prefixes, rejects a different equally long prefix, and leaves through the longest matching route.
inventory.distinction: A forwarding decision among overlapping route prefixes rather than insertion or word lookup in a trie.

inventory.label: Network Address Port Translation
inventory.definition: A translator maps private address and transport-port tuples to a shared public address with distinct ports, then reverses the mapping for replies.
inventory.motionThesis: Two UDP clients using the same source port acquire different external ports, and replies follow those table entries back to their original clients.
inventory.distinction: Transport-port demultiplexing between address realms, rather than link-layer discovery or encryption.

inventory.label: IPv4 Fragmentation
inventory.definition: IPv4 fragmentation divides a datagram into separately headed pieces whose offsets support reassembly at the destination.
inventory.motionThesis: A 1,500-byte payload splits into 600, 600, and 300 bytes for a 620-byte MTU and reassembles from out-of-order fragments at offsets 0, 75, and 150.
inventory.distinction: Packet size adaptation preserving all payload bytes; the fixture uses 20-byte headers, DF zero, eight-byte offset units, and destination reassembly.

inventory.label: Token-Bucket Rate Limiting
inventory.definition: A token bucket admits packets against credit that replenishes at a bounded rate up to a fixed capacity.
inventory.motionThesis: A four-token bucket admits four of five burst packets, refills two credits, then admits two of the next three packets while excess packets drop.
inventory.distinction: A single-bucket packet policer with clock-based refill, rather than consumer-demand feedback or a waiting queue.

inventory.label: Weighted Fair Queueing
inventory.definition: Weighted fair queueing approximates weighted byte-service shares by scheduling packets in virtual finish-time order.
inventory.motionThesis: Two queues with weights one and two compete by finish tags, with a double-length packet occupying twice the output width and transmission time.
inventory.distinction: Finish-tag scheduling with variable packet lengths, rather than round-robin packet counts or token admission policing.

inventory.label: De-Jitter Buffer
inventory.definition: A de-jitter buffer delays arriving media packets to absorb bounded arrival variation and provide regularly timed playout.
inventory.motionThesis: Uneven and briefly out-of-order arrivals wait in timestamp slots before leaving at uniform twenty-millisecond intervals.
inventory.distinction: Contrasts variable network arrival times with regular media playout; finite buffering cannot repair arbitrarily late arrivals.

inventory.label: Ethernet Collision Backoff
inventory.definition: Legacy shared half-duplex Ethernet aborts detected collisions and retries after random slot delays drawn from an expanding range.
inventory.motionThesis: Two transmitters collide, choose the same one-slot retry and collide again, then choose zero and three slots and succeed after carrier sensing.
inventory.distinction: A contention-and-retry fixture for shared half-duplex Ethernet, not modern switched full-duplex links; random choice ranges expand but actual delays need not double.

inventory.label: Spanning Tree Protocol
inventory.definition: Spanning Tree Protocol elects a root bridge and forwarding port roles while blocking redundant paths to prevent Layer 2 loops.
inventory.motionThesis: A triangle blocks the redundant port at one endpoint, then a link failure changes the root path and enables that port after convergence.
inventory.distinction: Distributed root and port-role selection with a failure transition, rather than global minimum-spanning-tree edge sorting; convergence timing is schematic.

inventory.label: Raft Consensus
inventory.definition: Raft elects a term-scoped leader that replicates an ordered log and commits eligible entries after majority replication.
inventory.motionThesis: A new leader copies a current-term entry to a majority, commits it, then communicates that commitment while a slower follower catches up.
inventory.distinction: Elected leadership and ordered replicated logs; followers learn commitment after the leader establishes it, rather than treating an append acknowledgment as commitment.

inventory.label: Quorum Read/Write Intersection
inventory.definition: Read and write quorum sizes can ensure each read set overlaps a completed write set so versioned replies expose that write.
inventory.motionThesis: A three-replica write and a three-replica read overlap within five replicas, and the shared replica supplies version two despite two stale read replies.
inventory.distinction: Set intersection with version selection in a fixed-membership fixture without concurrent writes; the inequality alone does not establish general linearizability.

inventory.label: Two-Phase Commit
inventory.definition: Two-phase commit first collects prepared votes from every transaction participant, then communicates a durable commit or abort decision.
inventory.motionThesis: Both participants lock in prepared state, the coordinator waits for both yes votes and records commit, then sends the decision that releases each participant.
inventory.distinction: Transaction unanimity and prepared locks rather than consensus by majority; a prepared participant cannot decide commit on its own.

inventory.label: Vector Clocks
inventory.definition: Vector clocks use per-process logical counters and componentwise comparisons to describe causal order and concurrent events.
inventory.motionThesis: Two incomparable send vectors meet at a third process, whose receive merges and local increments precede a reply that advances the first process.
inventory.distinction: Per-event causal vectors with receive increments, unlike a grow-only counter that merges contributions without incrementing on receipt.

inventory.label: Grow-Only Counter CRDT
inventory.definition: A grow-only counter stores per-replica increments, merges each component by maximum, and returns their sum.
inventory.motionThesis: Three replicas contribute two, one, and three increments, exchange missing components, and converge to six while a duplicate merge adds nothing.
inventory.distinction: Idempotent state merge and a numeric total; received state does not increment a local event clock and the object supports no decrement.

inventory.label: Consistent Hashing
inventory.definition: Consistent hashing assigns keys to servers in a hash space while limiting reassignment when membership changes.
inventory.motionThesis: Adding a server to a successor hash ring captures two nearby keys while their hash positions and all other owners stay fixed.
inventory.distinction: Membership-driven key ownership with wraparound, rather than address-prefix matching; a small ring is not guaranteed perfectly balanced.

inventory.label: Gossip Dissemination
inventory.definition: Gossip disseminates updates through repeated local exchanges between selected peers.
inventory.motionThesis: An update spreads across six equal peers over three illustrative rounds, including duplicate contacts that do not create another update.
inventory.distinction: Decentralized peer relays with redundant contacts rather than a broker; this selected contact schedule is not an unconditional delivery guarantee.

inventory.label: Stream Backpressure
inventory.definition: Demand-based stream backpressure limits upstream element emission to the credit requested by a downstream consumer.
inventory.motionThesis: The consumer requests two elements, pauses emission at zero credit, then requests one and two more to release the remaining three elements.
inventory.distinction: Application demand arrives from the consumer; credit does not refill on a clock and counts elements rather than TCP byte sequence space.

inventory.label: Publish-Subscribe
inventory.definition: Topic-based publish-subscribe delivers publisher events through a broker to matching subscriptions.
inventory.motionThesis: Three MQTT topic events route to exact, single-level wildcard, or multilevel wildcard subscribers, with copies delivered to every matching subscription.
inventory.distinction: Central topic matching and fanout rather than peer gossip or competing-consumer load balancing; the loss-free fixture does not imply exactly-once delivery.

inventory.label: Work-Stealing Scheduler
inventory.definition: A work-stealing scheduler balances parallel execution by letting an idle worker take queued tasks from a busy worker.
inventory.motionThesis: An owner takes the newest task from one end of a deque while an idle worker steals the oldest from the other, then both finish a second task without duplication.
inventory.distinction: A common owner-LIFO and thief-FIFO policy; tasks move only while queued, rather than being stolen during execution.

inventory.label: Write-Ahead Logging
inventory.definition: Write-ahead logging persists records describing changes before writing corresponding changed data pages, enabling recovery by replay.
inventory.motionThesis: A committed after-image reaches the durable log while the data page remains old, then a crash discards memory and replay restores the page to fifteen.
inventory.distinction: A synchronous committed transaction with idempotent SET replay; memory may change before log flush and the fixture makes no general undo claim.

inventory.label: LSM-Tree Compaction
inventory.definition: LSM-tree compaction merges sorted immutable runs while resolving key versions and reclaiming obsolete records when safe.
inventory.motionThesis: A newer value replaces an older duplicate and a tombstone removes its covered value while surviving keys merge into a fresh sorted run.
inventory.distinction: Version and deletion resolution rather than ordinary merge sorting; tombstone removal assumes bottommost full overlap, no snapshots, and no other older data.

inventory.label: Least-Recently-Used Cache
inventory.definition: An LRU cache refreshes recency on access and evicts the least recently accessed resident entry when a capacity miss requires room.
inventory.motionThesis: Requests A, B, C, A, D, and B reorder a three-entry cache, with the A hit protecting it while later misses evict B then C.
inventory.distinction: Access order rather than insertion order or frequency; the hit visibly changes which record is evicted.

inventory.label: Tracing Garbage Collection
inventory.definition: Tracing garbage collection finds objects reachable from program roots and reclaims unreachable heap objects.
inventory.motionThesis: Marking follows a rooted chain with a reachable cycle, then a sweep frees a separate unreachable cycle and an isolated object.
inventory.distinction: Memory reclamation after reachability tracing, rather than graph traversal alone; the illustrated mark-and-sweep collector does not compact objects or use reference counts.

inventory.label: Pipeline Data Hazard
inventory.definition: A pipeline data hazard occurs when an overlapped instruction requires an earlier instruction result before that result is available.
inventory.motionThesis: A load-use dependency holds an add in decode for one cycle, inserts a bubble, then forwards the loaded seven to execute an addition yielding twelve.
inventory.distinction: A specific five-stage pipeline with forwarding and a one-cycle load-use interlock, rather than a universal stall count for every processor.

inventory.label: Cardiac Valve Cycle
inventory.definition: Pressure-operated cardiac valves coordinate with chamber contraction to direct blood through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
inventory.motionThesis: Atrial filling and contraction precede ventricular contraction, with inlet closure, an all-closed interval, outlet opening, and relaxation shown in order.
inventory.distinction: Four chamber-specific valves and pressure-dependent flow phases; inlet and outlet valves do not open together on one side.

inventory.label: Venous Muscle Pump
inventory.definition: Skeletal-muscle contraction compresses veins while one-way valves help direct blood toward the heart.
inventory.motionThesis: Muscles narrow a venous segment, closing its lower valve and opening its upper valve to expel blood upward, then relax as it refills from below.
inventory.distinction: An externally compressed vein with passive one-way valves rather than an independently contracting heart.

inventory.label: Diaphragmatic Ventilation
inventory.definition: Diaphragm contraction enlarges the thoracic cavity and helps draw air into the lungs.
inventory.motionThesis: The diaphragm descends and flattens as the lungs expand and air enters, then rises during passive recoil and expiration.
inventory.distinction: Coupled thoracic volume change and airflow; quiet expiration is not an active downward squeeze.

inventory.label: Alveolar Gas Exchange
inventory.definition: Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse in opposite directions across the thin barrier between alveolar air and pulmonary blood.
inventory.motionThesis: Oxygen pairs leave the air sac as carbon-dioxide triads enter it, while a blood cell remains inside the adjacent capillary and becomes oxygenated.
inventory.distinction: Opposed molecular diffusion across two intact thin boundaries, rather than blood cells or gas bubbles crossing the barrier.

inventory.label: Alveolar Surfactant
inventory.definition: Pulmonary surfactant lowers surface tension and helps maintain alveolar stability as lung volume changes.
inventory.motionThesis: Two schematic air sacs experience inward compression, while surfactant molecules crowd a shrinking interface whose lumen stays wider than the comparison sac.
inventory.distinction: A qualitative surface-tension comparison, not a quantitative lung simulation or a rigid scaffold that guarantees prevention of collapse.

inventory.label: Mucociliary Escalator
inventory.definition: Coordinated airway cilia move mucus and trapped material toward the throat.
inventory.motionThesis: Cilia execute strong contacting strokes and bent recovery strokes in sequence, carrying a mucus layer and its trapped specks in one direction.
inventory.distinction: Asymmetric metachronal ciliary transport rather than symmetric pendulum motion or rotation of rigid propellers.

inventory.label: Swallowing Airway Protection
inventory.definition: Swallowing coordinates throat structures to guide a food bolus into the esophagus while protecting the airway.
inventory.motionThesis: The tongue advances a bolus as the larynx elevates and closes, the epiglottis folds, and the bolus passes behind the protected airway before breathing resumes.
inventory.distinction: Coordinated airway closure and posterior esophageal passage; the epiglottis is not the only protective structure.

inventory.label: Intestinal Segmentation
inventory.definition: Alternating intestinal contractions mix contents locally and increase their contact with the absorptive lining.
inventory.motionThesis: Paired constrictions alternate with a central constriction, redistributing substantial content patches in both directions with little net progression.
inventory.distinction: Local alternating mixing rather than a single downstream-traveling peristaltic wave.

inventory.label: Villus Nutrient Absorption
inventory.definition: Intestinal villi transfer absorbed nutrients toward blood capillaries and lymphatic lacteals.
inventory.motionThesis: Small absorbed nutrients enter a capillary loop while lipid-derived material is packaged in epithelial cells and enters the separate blind-ended lacteal.
inventory.distinction: Two anatomically separate transport routes with epithelial packaging, rather than whole dietary fat globules entering blood directly.

inventory.label: Glomerular Filtration
inventory.definition: Glomerular capillaries filter water and small solutes into the nephron while retaining blood cells and most proteins.
inventory.motionThesis: Small solutes cross the capillary barrier into capsule space and leave through a tubule while larger blood components remain in the vascular route.
inventory.distinction: Size-selective filtration with separate vascular and urinary exits; useful substances are also filtered and can be reabsorbed later.

inventory.label: Nephron Countercurrent Multiplier
inventory.definition: Different transport properties along the loop of Henle help establish a concentration gradient in the kidney medulla.
inventory.motionThesis: Opposed tubular flows accompany water loss from the descending limb and salt transport from a thick ascending segment as the surrounding gradient strengthens.
inventory.distinction: A simplified permeability-and-transport mechanism; the thick ascending limb does not release water and flow direction alone cannot create the gradient.

inventory.label: Micturition Reflex
inventory.definition: Bladder stretch contributes to neural coordination of bladder contraction and outlet relaxation during urination, subject to higher and voluntary control.
inventory.motionThesis: Filling stretches the bladder wall, a neural loop precedes outlet relaxation, and coordinated wall contraction empties the sac before the outlet closes.
inventory.distinction: Coordinated neural and muscular emptying rather than a passive overflow valve; stretch is not the sole determinant of urination.

inventory.label: Sliding Filament Contraction
inventory.definition: Muscle shortens when myosin cross-bridges pull actin filaments past thick filaments.
inventory.motionThesis: Staggered attaching and pivoting heads draw fixed-length thin filaments inward as Z-discs approach while the thick filament keeps its length.
inventory.distinction: Relative filament sliding rather than shortening either filament or shrinking the A-band; cross-bridge cycling includes detachment.

inventory.label: Antagonistic Elbow Muscles
inventory.definition: Opposing muscle groups alternately flex and extend the elbow through tension transmitted by tendons.
inventory.motionThesis: The forearm pivots about a fixed elbow while one muscle shortens and thickens, its antagonist lengthens, and both tendon insertions stay attached to the moving bone.
inventory.distinction: A simplified antagonistic pair with fixed attachment geometry; muscles exert pulling force rather than pushing bones.

inventory.label: Bone Remodeling
inventory.definition: Coordinated bone resorption and deposition continually replace existing bone tissue.
inventory.motionThesis: A multinucleated osteoclast excavates a pit and departs, then separate osteoblasts refill that same site with matrix that mineralizes progressively.
inventory.distinction: Localized tissue turnover without a fracture; osteoclasts do not transform into osteoblasts and newly secreted matrix is not instantly mineralized.

inventory.label: Fracture Repair
inventory.definition: Fractured bone repairs through overlapping hematoma, callus, mineralization, and remodeling processes.
inventory.motionThesis: A jagged gap gains a hematoma and soft bridge, develops mineralized callus, and regains cortical continuity as excess callus recedes.
inventory.distinction: Healing tissue bridges a fixed fracture gap rather than bone ends sliding together or welding instantly; the stages overlap.

inventory.label: Evaporative Thermoregulation
inventory.definition: Evaporation of sweat transfers heat from the skin to the environment.
inventory.motionThesis: A coiled gland delivers sweat to the surface, where escaping vapor accompanies a local cooling change.
inventory.distinction: Cooling follows evaporation rather than sweat production alone; the scene assumes conditions that permit evaporation.

inventory.label: Insulin-Mediated Glucose Uptake
inventory.definition: Insulin signaling increases surface GLUT4 transporters in muscle and adipose cells, supporting glucose uptake.
inventory.motionThesis: Insulin binds a receptor, an intracellular vesicle fuses with the membrane, and glucose then crosses through the inserted transporters.
inventory.distinction: The insulin receptor and GLUT4 carrier are separate proteins; this regulated route does not represent every tissue or all glucose uptake.

inventory.label: Hemoglobin Oxygen Loading
inventory.definition: Hemoglobin reversibly binds up to four oxygen molecules and supports oxygen delivery from lungs to tissues.
inventory.motionThesis: Four heme sites fill in an oxygen-rich setting, then two release intact oxygen molecules as the surrounding availability decreases.
inventory.distinction: A schematic occupancy cycle inside a red cell rather than free hemoglobin, oxygen splitting, or a quantitative binding curve.

inventory.label: Bile Emulsification
inventory.definition: Bile components help disperse dietary fat into smaller droplets that expose more surface to digestive enzymes.
inventory.motionThesis: Amphipathic surface symbols surround a large fat globule as mixing stretches it into several separately coated droplets.
inventory.distinction: Physical dispersion preserves the depicted fat area; it does not cut chemical bonds or depict lipase digestion, and the symbols abstract bile components.

inventory.label: Pupillary Light Reflex
inventory.definition: Light entering one eye normally produces constriction of both pupils through bilateral neural pathways.
inventory.motionThesis: A beam enters one eye, then both dark pupil apertures narrow after a short delay while the outer eyes and irises stay fixed.
inventory.distinction: Bilateral direct and consensual responses to unilateral light, with no claim that the dark aperture is itself a muscle.

inventory.label: Lens Accommodation
inventory.definition: Ciliary muscle contraction reduces zonular tension so the lens becomes more convex for near vision.
inventory.motionThesis: An approaching object sends more divergent rays, ciliary supports move inward, and a thicker lens redirects the rays to the same retinal point.
inventory.distinction: The retina stays fixed and the lens changes curvature as tension falls; the drawing simplifies ray optics and omits convergence.

inventory.label: Cochlear Tonotopy
inventory.definition: Different sound frequencies produce traveling-wave peaks at different positions along the cochlear basilar membrane.
inventory.motionThesis: Waves progress from the narrow base toward the wider apex, with a high-frequency peak near the base and a lower-frequency peak farther along.
inventory.distinction: A spatially delayed traveling wave with a growing and then decaying envelope rather than a standing string or a scanning isolated peak.

inventory.label: Semicircular Canal Sensing
inventory.definition: Semicircular canals sense head rotation through transient endolymph-driven cupula deflection and associated hair-bundle bending.
inventory.motionThesis: Head rotation begins, fluid briefly lags and bends the cupula, adaptation reduces the bend during steady rotation, and stopping reverses it transiently.
inventory.distinction: A time-compressed transient angular-motion response rather than sustained counterrotation or gravity sensing.

inventory.label: Patellar Stretch Reflex
inventory.definition: A brief tendon-induced stretch activates quadriceps muscle spindles and spinal circuitry that contracts quadriceps to extend the knee.
inventory.motionThesis: A tap below the kneecap stretches a spindle in the thigh, a sensory signal reaches the spinal cord, and a motor return precedes knee extension.
inventory.distinction: The illustrated excitatory reflex path is monosynaptic; the spindle is in muscle and the fuller reflex includes antagonist inhibition.

inventory.label: Saltatory Conduction
inventory.definition: Electrical current spreads under myelin while action potentials regenerate at exposed nodes of Ranvier.
inventory.motionThesis: A node activates, subdued current spreads along a continuous axon under the next myelin sleeve, and the following node activates as its predecessor becomes refractory.
inventory.distinction: Axial current and local regeneration rather than sparks crossing empty gaps or individual ions traveling the length of the axon.

inventory.label: Crossed Extensor Reflex
inventory.definition: Spinal pathways coordinate withdrawal from a painful limb stimulus with contralateral extension that supports posture.
inventory.motionThesis: Contact beneath one foot precedes sensory and crossed spinal signals, after which that leg flexes while the opposite extensor activates over a planted foot.
inventory.distinction: A simplified polysynaptic bilateral response rather than the monosynaptic stretch reflex or simultaneous withdrawal of both legs.

inventory.label: Pacinian Adaptation
inventory.definition: Pacinian corpuscles respond strongly to changing deformation and adapt rapidly during a sustained stimulus.
inventory.motionThesis: A pad depresses nested lamellae, a brief axonal burst subsides during the held indentation, and pad release produces another brief response.
inventory.distinction: Qualitative mechanical filtering with onset and offset responses rather than sustained firing or nerve exhaustion.

inventory.label: Retinal Center-Surround Response
inventory.definition: In a classic ON-center retinal ganglion cell, central light increases firing while illumination of the surrounding region opposes that response.
inventory.motionThesis: The same axon shows baseline, increased, suppressed, and modest firing during darkness, central illumination, annular illumination, and uniform illumination.
inventory.distinction: A functional receptive-field diagram rather than a cell membrane; the selected ON-center response does not describe every ganglion cell.

inventory.label: Vestibulo-Ocular Reflex
inventory.definition: Vestibular reflex pathways produce compensatory eye movements that help stabilize gaze during head movement.
inventory.motionThesis: A head oscillates beneath a fixed target while both eyes rotate relative to it so their world-space gaze lines remain aimed at that target.
inventory.distinction: Compensatory eye rotation rather than pupil translation or a sustained nystagmus reset; the diagram omits pathway detail.

inventory.label: Hemostatic Plug
inventory.definition: Platelet adhesion and aggregation at vascular injury form a plug that is reinforced by coagulation-generated fibrin.
inventory.motionThesis: A wall defect leaks, arriving platelets activate and accumulate, and a separate fibrin mesh reinforces the local seal while the lumen stays open.
inventory.distinction: Platelets and fibrin retain separate identities, with overlapping stages and continued passage through the vessel.

inventory.label: Phagocytosis
inventory.definition: A phagocyte encloses a particle in a phagosome that can interact with lysosomal compartments for degradation.
inventory.motionThesis: Pseudopods surround a microbe, enclosure produces a distinct phagosome, and subsequent lysosome fusion precedes fragmentation inside it.
inventory.distinction: The membrane changes topology and the cargo stays outside the nucleus; the illustrated successful degradation is not guaranteed for all microbes.

inventory.label: Antibody Neutralization
inventory.definition: Antibodies that bind particular pathogen or toxin epitopes can block attachment to target cells.
inventory.motionThesis: A Fab tip docks on a viral attachment spike, and the bound antibody obstructs that interface as the intact complex approaches a cellular receptor.
inventory.distinction: Specific attachment blockade rather than agglutination, phagocytosis, or universal protection by any antibody.

inventory.label: Leukocyte Diapedesis
inventory.definition: Leukocytes adhere to vascular endothelium and cross it to enter surrounding tissue.
inventory.motionThesis: A rolling cell arrests at a junction, extends through it, draws its deforming nucleus and cell body across, and leaves the junction to close behind it.
inventory.distinction: A paracellular example with continued red-cell flow above; not every transmigration route passes between endothelial cells.

inventory.label: Clonal Selection
inventory.definition: Appropriate activation selects lymphocytes with matching antigen specificity and promotes expansion of that population.
inventory.motionThesis: An antigen fits one of three receptor motifs, a separate activation cue follows, and only the matching cell divides into descendants with the same motif.
inventory.distinction: Selection of an existing specificity rather than antigen-directed receptor redesign; supporting activation signals are abbreviated.

inventory.label: Immunological Memory
inventory.definition: Persistent antigen-specific memory cells support a faster, often stronger response to subsequent exposure to the same antigen.
inventory.motionThesis: A first encounter produces a delayed small effector group and a surviving memory cell, then the same antigen returns and a shorter delay precedes a larger secretory response.
inventory.distinction: Persistence across two encounters rather than selection among receptor types; duration and protection vary, and the second response is not instantaneous.

inventory.label: Balloon-Expanded Stent
inventory.definition: Inflation of a balloon catheter expands a mounted stent against an arterial narrowing, leaving the stent in place after catheter removal.
inventory.motionThesis: A compressed mesh reaches a narrowed lumen, expands with the balloon as plaque deforms, and remains expanded while the balloon deflates and withdraws.
inventory.distinction: A retained open mesh rather than a solid sleeve; plaque remains present and blood does not traverse the inflated balloon.

inventory.label: Hemodialysis Membrane Exchange
inventory.definition: A dialyzer allows selected small solutes to exchange between blood and dialysis solution across a separating membrane.
inventory.motionThesis: Blood and dialysis solution flow oppositely along a hollow fiber while illustrated waste solutes diffuse outward and red cells remain within the blood route.
inventory.distinction: A solute-diffusion example, not fluid mixing or pressure-driven ultrafiltration; other solutes can have different gradients.

inventory.label: Re-Epithelialization
inventory.definition: Epithelial cells migrate and proliferate to restore coverage of an injured surface.
inventory.motionThesis: Leading cells flatten and advance from both epithelial margins across a wound bed, followers replenish the sheet, and the meeting surface gains thickness.
inventory.distinction: Surface coverage rather than whole-wound contraction, teleporting cells, or a depiction of all deeper tissue repair.

inventory.label: Sprouting Angiogenesis
inventory.definition: Endothelial sprouts extend from existing vessels and can connect to establish new vascular pathways.
inventory.motionThesis: Attached tips extend filopodia as stalks grow, the two sprouts meet, a continuous lumen forms, and only then does a red cell cross the connection.
inventory.distinction: Sprouting and anastomosis rather than an isolated vessel appearing or blood flowing through a blind tip; vascular growth has other forms.

inventory.label: Replication Fork
inventory.definition: DNA unwinding exposes parental templates for continuous leading-strand and discontinuous lagging-strand synthesis.
inventory.motionThesis: A fork advances as one new strand extends toward it while successive fragments extend away from it before primer replacement and nick sealing.
inventory.distinction: Both new strands grow five-prime to three-prime; the parental strands stay continuous, and ligase seals a nick after gap filling.

inventory.label: DNA Transcription
inventory.definition: RNA polymerase builds an RNA strand complementary to one DNA template strand.
inventory.motionThesis: A moving polymerase opens a local DNA bubble, elongates a trailing RNA at its bound three-prime end, and releases it as the DNA reanneals.
inventory.distinction: One RNA product from one template rather than two daughter DNA molecules; a bacterial schematic omits eukaryotic processing.

inventory.label: RNA Splicing
inventory.definition: Spliceosomal processing removes an intron and joins its flanking exons.
inventory.motionThesis: An intron folds into a branched lariat after the first cleavage, then exon ligation releases the loop-and-tail intron and leaves a joined RNA chain.
inventory.distinction: Two ordered RNA reactions rather than DNA excision or removal of all noncoding sequence; retained exons need not all encode protein.

inventory.label: Ribosomal Translation
inventory.definition: A ribosome decodes messenger RNA through transfer RNAs and extends a polypeptide.
inventory.motionThesis: A charged A-site tRNA accepts the P-site peptide, then tRNAs and intact mRNA translocate by one codon as the empty E-site tRNA exits.
inventory.distinction: One elongation cycle with peptide transfer before translocation, rather than a whole protein being completed or free amino acids attaching directly.

inventory.label: Lac Operon Induction
inventory.definition: Allolactose binding reduces the lac repressor’s operator affinity, permitting increased transcription under appropriate regulatory conditions.
inventory.motionThesis: An inducer changes repressor binding geometry and releases the operator, allowing polymerase to advance while an upstream activation cue remains present.
inventory.distinction: A specified low-glucose activating context; derepression alone is not maximal activation, and basal expression can occur before induction.

inventory.label: Nucleosome Packaging
inventory.definition: A DNA duplex wraps around a histone core to form a repeating unit of chromatin.
inventory.motionThesis: Exposed linker contour feeds into partial turns around an existing eight-part histone core, then relaxes slightly while both DNA backbones remain continuous.
inventory.distinction: A nucleosome with approximately one and two-thirds turns rather than a generic single-strand spool; linker histone H1 is not part of the core octamer.

inventory.label: Polymerase Chain Reaction
inventory.definition: Repeated denaturation, primer annealing, and primer extension amplify a selected DNA segment.
inventory.motionThesis: A bounded duplex separates into templates, primers bind opposite ends, and five-prime-to-three-prime extension produces two duplexes before a repeat produces four.
inventory.distinction: Idealized amplification beginning with an already bounded product, rather than a claim of exact target-length products in the first genomic-template cycle.

inventory.label: DNA Gel Electrophoresis
inventory.definition: An electric field separates DNA fragments through a porous gel, with shorter linear fragments usually migrating farther during the same run.
inventory.motionThesis: Populations leave shared wells toward the positive electrode and separate into sample and reference-ladder bands at different distances.
inventory.distinction: Visible bands contain many stained molecules; distance rather than band width encodes size, and co-migration does not establish sequence identity.

inventory.label: Restriction-Ligation Cloning
inventory.definition: Compatible restriction-generated DNA ends are joined by ligase to assemble recombinant DNA.
inventory.motionThesis: Two staggered cuts release a plasmid segment, a contrasting insert pairs with the exposed ends, and sealing both strands completes the recombinant circle.
inventory.distinction: Compatible-end annealing precedes covalent ligation; the result alone does not demonstrate transformation or gene expression.

inventory.label: CRISPR-Cas9 Targeting
inventory.definition: A guide RNA directs Cas9 to a compatible DNA target adjacent to a PAM, where the complex can cleave both DNA strands.
inventory.motionThesis: PAM engagement precedes an expanding guide-DNA hybrid and displaced strand, followed by two cuts whose ends remain clamped until enzyme withdrawal.
inventory.distinction: Targeted cleavage rather than guaranteed precise repair; the PAM is in the DNA, and the unlettered diagram does not assert an exact nucleotide offset.

inventory.label: Mitotic Chromosome Segregation
inventory.definition: Sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite spindle poles during mitosis.
inventory.motionThesis: Three bioriented chromosomes split into continuous sister chromatids whose pole-facing centromeres lead while attached spindle fibers shorten.
inventory.distinction: Each destination receives one copy of each represented chromosome; separating chromatids is distinct from cytokinesis.

inventory.label: Meiotic Reduction
inventory.definition: Homolog separation in meiosis I reduces chromosome-set number while sister chromatids remain paired.
inventory.motionThesis: Two homolog pairs segregate as intact duplicated chromosomes, giving each nascent nucleus one long and one short chromosome with sister chromatids still joined.
inventory.distinction: The unit separated is a homolog rather than a sister chromatid; only meiosis I is shown, with no intervening replication or four-gamete result.

inventory.label: Meiotic Crossing Over
inventory.definition: Homologous nonsister chromatids exchange corresponding DNA segments during meiotic prophase I.
inventory.motionThesis: The inner two chromatids of a tetrad form an exchange junction and resolve into reciprocal combinations while the outer sisters retain their original segments.
inventory.distinction: One illustrated reciprocal crossover produces two recombinant and two nonrecombinant chromatids rather than whole-chromosome exchange.

inventory.label: Bacterial Conjugation
inventory.definition: Direct contact allows a donor bacterium to transfer DNA to a recipient through conjugation machinery.
inventory.motionThesis: A pilus establishes contact, a plasmid strand threads through a bridge, and replacement and complementary synthesis leave a duplex plasmid in each cell.
inventory.distinction: An F-plasmid example with both chromosomes retained and donor copy maintained, rather than binary fission or transfer of an intact rigid ring.

inventory.label: Apoptotic Fragmentation
inventory.definition: During apoptosis a cell condenses and can partition into membrane-enclosed bodies for clearance.
inventory.motionThesis: A shrinking cell condenses chromatin, develops connected blebs with narrowing necks, and separates into closed bodies that retain their contents.
inventory.distinction: A common morphological sequence rather than lytic bursting; bodies need not all contain nuclear material and clearance can begin earlier.

inventory.label: Macroautophagy
inventory.definition: A double-membrane autophagosome encloses cytoplasmic material and delivers it for lysosomal degradation.
inventory.motionThesis: A cup closes around internal cargo, its outer membrane fuses with a lysosome, and the retained inner membrane and cargo are subsequently degraded.
inventory.distinction: Intracellular sequestration rather than extracellular phagocytosis, with outer-membrane fusion preceding inner-membrane breakdown.

inventory.label: Kinesin Cargo Transport
inventory.definition: A processive kinesin dimer uses ATP-linked head coordination to carry cargo along a microtubule.
inventory.motionThesis: Alternating rear heads pass the bound leading head, advancing a continuously tethered vesicle along a polar track.
inventory.distinction: Conventional plus-end-directed kinesin rather than a claim about every kinesin or two heads sliding together.

inventory.label: ATP Synthase Rotary Catalysis
inventory.definition: Ion-gradient-driven rotor motion couples to catalytic conformational changes that synthesize ATP.
inventory.motionThesis: Proton translocation turns a membrane rotor and central shaft while stationary catalytic sites cycle through binding, synthesis, and release.
inventory.distinction: The rotor turns inside a stator; protons power conformational change rather than becoming ATP, and no fixed ion-to-ATP ratio is asserted.

inventory.label: Sodium-Potassium Pump
inventory.definition: ATP-linked conformational changes typically export three sodium ions and import two potassium ions per transport cycle.
inventory.motionThesis: An inward-facing pocket binds three sodium ions, switches access to release them outside, and returns two potassium ions to the cytoplasm.
inventory.distinction: Alternating access rather than an open channel or simultaneous five-ion crossing; phosphorylation is shown on the cytoplasmic domain.

inventory.label: Plant Cell Plasmolysis
inventory.definition: Water loss in a hypertonic environment can shrink a plant protoplast away from its cell wall.
inventory.motionThesis: Net outward water movement reduces vacuole and protoplast size while the wall stays fixed and organelles remain inside the withdrawing membrane.
inventory.distinction: The extracellular solution occupies the wall-membrane gap; external solute remains outside and the wall does not shrink.

inventory.label: Stomatal Turgor
inventory.definition: Changes in guard-cell water status and wall mechanics alter the stomatal pore.
inventory.motionThesis: Water entry expands kidney-shaped guard cells and bows their inner walls apart before water loss closes the aperture.
inventory.distinction: An angiosperm stoma with deforming walls and anchored tips, not two rigid cells translating or a universal response across all plants.

inventory.label: Phototropic Growth
inventory.definition: Unequal growth across a shoot produces curvature toward directional light.
inventory.motionThesis: Directional light precedes stronger shaded-side elongation, increasing cell lengths and bending the growing shoot toward the source.
inventory.distinction: Distributed differential shoot growth rather than rigid hinge rotation or leaf tracking; root responses need not follow this pattern.

inventory.label: Xylem Cohesion-Tension
inventory.definition: Evaporation from leaves generates tension transmitted through cohesive xylem water, supporting upward transport.
inventory.motionThesis: Evaporation deepens a leaf-surface meniscus while tracers advance upward within a continuously filled water column.
inventory.distinction: Transpiration-driven tension rather than a root piston or a claim that capillary rise alone supports tall-tree transport.

inventory.label: Phloem Pressure Flow
inventory.definition: A hydrostatic pressure difference drives bulk phloem flow from a source region toward a sink.
inventory.motionThesis: Source sugar loading recruits water, mixed sap moves through sieve-plate openings, and sink unloading permits water return.
inventory.distinction: A source-above and sink-below example rather than universally downward phloem flow or long-distance sugar diffusion alone.

inventory.label: Root-Nodule Nitrogen Fixation
inventory.definition: Rhizobial bacteroids in legume root nodules reduce atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia that supports plant nitrogen nutrition.
inventory.motionThesis: A nitrogen molecule enters a nodule bacteroid, separates into two ammonia products, and supplies the root while plant carbon arrives in the opposite direction.
inventory.distinction: Bacterial nitrogen fixation rather than nitrate uptake or a root splitting nitrogen; ATP, electron supply, and later assimilation are omitted from the schematic.

inventory.label: Mycorrhizal Exchange
inventory.definition: Mycorrhizal fungi acquire soil nutrients and exchange them for plant-derived carbon across a specialized root interface.
inventory.motionThesis: Phosphate travels through branching hyphae and crosses the arbuscular interface while a separate carbon cargo passes from the plant toward the fungus.
inventory.distinction: Arbuscular nutrient exchange with a host membrane surrounding fungal branches, not bacterial nitrogen fixation or a claim of altruistic root networks.

inventory.label: Pollen Tube Guidance
inventory.definition: Signals from ovular tissues steer a growing pollen tube toward the embryo sac for sperm delivery.
inventory.motionThesis: A tube lengthens only at its tip, curves toward a local synergid signal, and enters a real micropyle opening while its older shaft stays in place.
inventory.distinction: Guidance and tip growth rather than subsequent double fertilization; local LURE signaling is a species-specific example.

inventory.label: Angiosperm Double Fertilization
inventory.definition: Two sperm cells fuse separately with an egg and a central cell, initiating the embryo and endosperm.
inventory.motionThesis: Two delivered sperm follow separate routes and merge with one maternal egg nucleus or the two-nucleus central-cell complement, leaving distinct products.
inventory.distinction: A common angiosperm diploid-zygote and triploid-endosperm pattern, not two sperm fertilizing one egg.

inventory.label: Natural Selection
inventory.definition: Heritable variants change in frequency when their carriers contribute differently to subsequent generations.
inventory.motionThesis: More conspicuous moths are removed before breeding, and surviving pairs produce an offspring cohort with a higher dark-morph proportion.
inventory.distinction: A simplified heritable two-morph example with new offspring, not individuals changing color to meet a need or a full Mendelian cross.

inventory.label: Genetic Drift
inventory.definition: Finite-population sampling can change allele frequencies between generations even when the alleles have equal fitness.
inventory.motionThesis: Copies of stochastically sampled parental alleles form successive diploid cohorts whose composition changes without a survival advantage.
inventory.distinction: One recorded neutral inheritance realization, not selection, mutation of existing individuals, or a universal direction of change.

inventory.label: Allopatric Speciation
inventory.definition: Geographically separated populations can diverge until reproductive barriers persist even after contact is restored.
inventory.motionThesis: A barrier stops gene flow, isolated generations develop different courtship rhythms, and renewed contact leaves cross-lineage signals unmatched while within-lineage pairs reproduce.
inventory.distinction: An illustrative possible behavioral barrier, not a claim that every isolated population speciates or a historical firefly case.

inventory.label: Predator-Prey Cycle
inventory.definition: Feedback between prey availability and predation can produce population oscillations in which predator abundance follows prey abundance.
inventory.motionThesis: A sampled Lotka-Volterra cycle shows prey growth followed by predator increase, prey depletion, predator decline, and prey recovery.
inventory.distinction: An idealized population model with glyphs representing abundance units, not an individual chase or a claim that every ecosystem oscillates periodically.
