inventory.distinction: Bus inertia 9 and wheel inertia 1 give bus angle minus one tenth of relative wheel angle, conserving zero initial angular momentum; no external desaturation torque is modeled.

inventory.label: Thruster Docking
inventory.definition: Attitude-control thrusters adjust relative spacecraft motion for low-speed aligned docking.
inventory.motionThesis: Symmetric aft jets accelerate a chaser, a flame-free coast follows, and forward-facing jets brake it before the capture collar closes.
inventory.distinction: The local station-frame translation uses matched force pairs and a piecewise acceleration/coast/braking trajectory; orbital rendezvous and attitude errors are outside the fixture.

inventory.label: Gridded Ion Thruster
inventory.definition: A gridded ion thruster ionizes propellant and electrostatically accelerates positive ions through grids while neutralizing the outgoing beam.
inventory.motionThesis: Atoms enter an ionization chamber, positive ions accelerate through aligned grid apertures, and a separate external cathode supplies electrons downstream.
inventory.distinction: The cutaway tracks charge states and distinguishes ion optics from Hall propulsion; neutralization denotes beam charge balance rather than universal immediate recombination.

inventory.label: Aerobraking
inventory.definition: Aerobraking uses repeated upper-atmosphere drag passes to reduce orbital energy and lower apoapsis.
inventory.motionThesis: A spacecraft passes through a thin atmospheric shell near a shared periapsis and continues onto successively smaller-apoapsis orbits.
inventory.distinction: Three idealized osculating ellipses share a focus and periapsis, with changes confined to that point; Kepler timing is used within each ellipse and finite drag passes are compressed.

inventory.label: Ablative Heat Shield
inventory.definition: An ablative heat shield protects a vehicle through material decomposition, gas release and sacrificial surface loss.
inventory.motionThesis: The hot exposed face recedes into the material while the char boundary advances, gases leave outward and the backing remains comparatively cool.
inventory.distinction: The planar cutaway compresses a finite heating episode and separates recession from internal pyrolysis; no thermal certification or flight heat flux is implied.

inventory.label: Sky-Crane Landing
inventory.definition: A sky-crane descent stage lowers a rover on bridles and departs after the rover reaches the surface.
inventory.motionThesis: Three taut bridles lower the rover until its wheels contact terrain; the lines release only after touchdown and the powered stage flies away.
inventory.distinction: The sequence depicts the Mars rover landing architecture with exaggerated distances; bridles remain attached throughout lowering and no suspended rover is released early.

inventory.label: Webb Sunshield Deployment
inventory.definition: Webb deploys and tensions five separated sunshield membranes to protect its cold telescope from solar heating.
inventory.motionThesis: Support pallets open, opposed booms draw out folded membranes, and five distinct layers separate and become taut beneath the telescope.
inventory.distinction: The oblique schematic focuses on sunshield hardware rather than mirror-wing deployment; it compresses the multi-day sequence and does not model membrane stress.

inventory.label: Rocker-Bogie Suspension
inventory.definition: Rocker-bogie linkages allow rover wheels to articulate over uneven ground while supporting the vehicle.
inventory.motionThesis: Three wheels maintain terrain contact as a rigid bogie and rocker change angle across a rounded obstacle.
inventory.distinction: The kinematic one-side model solves wheel-normal contact and fixed link lengths; the body locates the rocker pivot but does not claim a solved opposite-side differential or equal wheel loads.

inventory.label: Exoplanet Transit Photometry
inventory.definition: Transit photometry measures the loss of unresolved stellar light when a planet crosses the visible stellar disc.
inventory.motionThesis: A planet crosses a bright star while a synchronized flux cursor traces curved ingress, a flat full-transit interval and egress.
inventory.distinction: A central transit across a uniformly bright star uses exact overlapping-circle area; radius ratio one quarter gives a 6.25 percent full-transit depth, with no limb darkening.

inventory.label: Radial-Velocity Planet Detection
inventory.definition: Periodic Doppler shifts in stellar spectral lines can reveal the star's reflex motion caused by an orbiting companion.
inventory.motionThesis: A small stellar wobble is measured as a coherent shift of absorption lines and a signed radial-velocity trace, with zero shift at maximum displacement.
inventory.distinction: The observer lies to the left; v is proportional to minus sine of orbital phase and all lines have the same fractional wavelength shift, exaggerated for legibility.

inventory.label: Astronomical Aperture Synthesis
inventory.definition: An interferometer combines measurements from antenna pairs to sample spatial frequencies and reconstruct sky brightness.
inventory.motionThesis: Three fixed antennas provide three baselines whose positive and negative spatial-frequency samples sweep conjugate arcs as the projected geometry rotates.
inventory.distinction: The pole-source idealization rotates projected baselines through a quarter turn; sparse arc coverage is not a filled physical dish or a complete reconstructed image.

inventory.label: Adaptive Optics
inventory.definition: Adaptive optics measures wavefront errors and adjusts a deformable mirror to reduce optical aberration.
inventory.motionThesis: A sensor detects a distorted wavefront, a feedback path drives mirror actuators, and residual wavefront corrugation decreases after the mirror responds.
inventory.distinction: Separate input, sensor and output views form an explanatory optical schematic; mirror height is minus half the corrected path error, and no full-system ray trace or perfect atmospheric correction is claimed.

inventory.label: Segmented-Mirror Phasing
inventory.definition: Segmented-mirror phasing adjusts optical path differences so separate mirror segments act coherently.
inventory.motionThesis: Three rigid segments remove their piston offsets, their reflected wavefront pieces align, and the on-axis coherence indicator increases.
inventory.distinction: The three equal segments start at reflected phases minus pi/2, zero and plus pi/2; the shown indicator is the squared magnitude of their mean complex field, not simply stacked image spots.

inventory.label: Touch-and-Go Asteroid Sampling
inventory.definition: A gas-driven touch-and-go sampler briefly contacts an asteroid and mobilizes regolith into a collection head.
inventory.motionThesis: A fixed-length sampling arm descends with its spacecraft, a gas pulse follows contact, and captured grains stay inside the head as it lifts away.
inventory.distinction: This OSIRIS-REx-style collection episode uses gas mobilization rather than drilling or vacuum suction; the vehicle body never lands on the surface.

inventory.label: Star-Tracker Attitude Determination
inventory.definition: A star tracker estimates spacecraft orientation by matching observed star directions to a catalog.
inventory.motionThesis: A fixed observed star pattern is matched to a rotated catalog pattern, then an attitude-axis readout reports the inferred roll.
inventory.distinction: The camera pattern rotated plus 25 degrees corresponds to minus 25 degrees of camera roll; this two-dimensional example illustrates correspondence; the output glyph is a measurement display, not a spacecraft being torqued by its sensor.

inventory.label: Aerogel Dust Capture
inventory.definition: Aerogel can decelerate incoming dust grains while preserving terminal material and penetration tracks for study.
inventory.motionThesis: A grain enters a translucent collector, slows along an increasingly long tapered track, and remains at the track's tip.
inventory.distinction: A cubic penetration history monotonically decreases speed inside the aerogel; one simple track is shown without implying that real grains never fragment.

inventory.label: Market Clearing
inventory.definition: A market-clearing price equates quantities supplied and demanded in a specified market model.
inventory.motionThesis: A low price attracts more buyers than sellers, a high price does the reverse, and a final intermediate price pairs two willing sellers with two willing buyers.
inventory.distinction: Seller reservations 2,4,6,8 and buyer reservations 9,7,5,3 produce shortage at 3, surplus at 7 and two trades at 5.5; this is a posted-price toy market, not a universal adjustment law.

inventory.label: Order Book Matching
inventory.definition: An exchange can match incoming orders against resting orders under price and time priority.
inventory.motionThesis: A buy order consumes two earlier tickets and then one later ticket at the best ask before the next buy reaches the higher-price queue.
inventory.distinction: The stated FIFO example has A100x2, B100x1 and C101x2; buys of three then one leave one ticket at 101, rather than implying every venue uses the same matching rule.

inventory.label: Comparative Advantage
inventory.definition: Comparative advantage is the ability to produce a good at lower opportunity cost than another producer.
inventory.motionThesis: Two workshops compare mixed production with specialization under the same labor budget, then exchange goods so each finishes with two food and two cloth units.
inventory.distinction: Per labor tick A makes two food or one cloth and B one food or two cloth; two-tick rounds yield mixed bundles 2F1C and 1F2C versus specialized 4F and 4C, traded at one for one.

inventory.label: Cobweb Price Dynamics
inventory.definition: Cobweb dynamics arise when production responds to earlier prices and current prices clear the resulting supply.
inventory.motionThesis: A staircase alternates from the previous price to a supply decision and then to the new demand-clearing price, converging with alternating overshoot.
inventory.distinction: The naive-expectation fixture uses demand P=10-Q and supply P=2Q, giving Q_t=P_(t-1)/2 and P_t=10-Q_t; these chosen slopes converge, unlike all possible cobweb models.

inventory.label: Bank Run
inventory.definition: Simultaneous withdrawals can force a bank to liquidate long-term investments before maturity at a loss.
inventory.motionThesis: Two liquid reserve coins pay the first depositors; pairs of term claims must then be sold for half value to fund two more withdrawals, leaving two claims unpaid.
inventory.distinction: Six unit deposits fund two cash units and four unit-maturity assets; early liquidation returns one half per asset, so total payout is four units in this illustrative liquidity mismatch.

inventory.label: Ascending Auction
inventory.definition: An English ascending auction raises bids until one bidder remains willing to make the winning bid.
inventory.motionThesis: Three bidders raise paddles at successively higher prices, drop out beyond their reservations and leave one bidder to receive the lot after the hammer falls.
inventory.distinction: Reservations are 4,7,10 and public bids are 2,4,6,8; the winner pays the final bid 8, not automatically their value 10 or the runner-up value 7.

inventory.label: Public Goods Free Riding
inventory.definition: A free rider enjoys a nonexcludable benefit without contributing to its provision.
inventory.motionThesis: Three households contribute to a shared streetlamp while a fourth retains its token but receives the same light; a second round with fewer contributions provides less light.
inventory.distinction: The nonrival light field is distinct from the funding tokens; the paired rounds illustrate a provision incentive rather than asserting that every person defects.

inventory.label: Common-Pool Governance
inventory.definition: Users can govern a subtractable shared resource through collectively maintained allocation rules and monitoring.
inventory.motionThesis: An upstream diversion first starves later plots, then a visible turn token rotates among four users while only its holder’s gate admits the next water allocation.
inventory.distinction: The irrigation example depicts one local rotation rule with finite allocations and peer visibility; it does not equate common property with unmanaged access or claim universal success.

inventory.label: Schelling Segregation Model
inventory.definition: Schelling’s model shows how local neighborhood preferences can produce aggregate residential clustering.
inventory.motionThesis: One dissatisfied household at a time moves into an acceptable vacancy, retaining all identities and leaving its former cell empty as clusters emerge.
inventory.distinction: A 6 by 6 toy grid contains fourteen households of each type and eight vacancies; dissatisfaction means less than 40 percent same-type occupied Moore neighbors, with asynchronous relocation. Deterministic fixture seed 1 performs 9 legal moves; it is not a full account of real segregation.

inventory.label: Bullwhip Effect
inventory.definition: The bullwhip effect is amplification of order variability upstream along a supply chain.
inventory.motionThesis: A small retail demand pulse produces progressively larger delayed order-ticket bursts through a four-stage chain, followed by under-ordering.
inventory.distinction: The disclosed fixture uses O_t=max(0,2d_t-d_(t-1)) with one-period message delay at each stage; these are requests, not conserved goods or a fitted inventory model.

retainedDistinctions: Stirling mechanism vs pressure-volume cycle: mechanism vs thermodynamic representation.
Bragg spectrometer vs diffraction: apparatus vs phenomenon.
Chladni figures vs membrane modes: different boundary conditions and media.
Anemometer vs Robinson instrument: general measurement vs specific hardware.
Harmonograph vs Lissajous: a physical damped drawing process can be distinct; redesign would be preferable to retirement.
